scan_metadata.notes: Fresh shallow clone of the default branch (depth 20), so has_uncommitted_changes reflects the clone (false), not the author's working copy. This is a QGIS desktop plugin (PyQt/qgis.core), not a web service: there are no routes or network listeners. Python code was read directly; 'qgis' and 'osgeo' imports are provided by the QGIS host and not declared in any manifest (metadata.txt declares qgisMinimumVersion 3.40 and maximum 4.99). Excluded: docs/ images, a .pptx, i18n .ts file, and docs/testing scratch scripts (reviewed only for paths and secrets). Version mismatch observed: metadata.txt is 0.6.5, README badge says 0.6.4, docs/TODO.md says 0.4.1.

what_this_app_can_do: Scans a user-selected folder tree for geospatial datasets and writes an inventory of files (format, CRS, size, metadata status) into a local GeoPackage.
Lets a QGIS user create and edit layer metadata through a 4-step wizard with contact and link management, and saves it to a local database cache, .qmd sidecar files, or embedded GeoPackage metadata.
Parses existing FGDC, ESRI, ISO 19115 and embedded metadata from local files to pre-fill forms.
Shows a metadata quality dashboard with completion statistics by directory, format and CRS.
Records the scanning user's OS username, machine hostname and OS version in the inventory records for multi-user tracking.

data_sources_touched.source: Local GeoPackage/SQLite inventory and metadata database (geospatial_inventory and related tables)
Local geospatial data files and metadata sidecars (shp, gpkg, FGDC/ESRI/ISO XML, .qmd)
data_sources_touched.access: read_write (reads datasets and metadata; writes .qmd and embedded metadata)

capability_summary.who_can_reach_it: Runs inside the user's own QGIS desktop session; no listener, no authentication and none needed. Anyone with filesystem access to the shared GeoPackage can read the inventory, including recorded usernames and hostnames.
unauthorized_action_red_flags: Records OS username and machine hostname of each scanner in the inventory database (personal/operational data stored without any stated consent or retention policy)
Writes metadata sidecar files and embedded metadata into the user's data directories
